title: Programmable Spin Conversion in Gradient Quantum Matter
authors: Mamoru Matsuo, Yuta Sekino, Hiroyuki Tajima
abstract: We propose programmable spin conversion in ultracold gases as gradient quantum matter, whose spin-dependent self-energy varies in space. Quantum kinetic theory shows that a dissipative self-energy curvature turns a force-driven scalar anisotropy into a spin source with mixed longitudinal-transverse momentum parity. Spin-resolved time-of-flight imaging can reveal a transverse spin texture that changes sign when either the drive or programmed curvature is reversed. Ultracold gases thereby offer a controllable spin source for gradient quantum matter.
summary: This work develops a quantum kinetic theory approach to model programmable spin conversion in gradient quantum matter using ultracold gases. By analyzing how spatially varying self-energies generate momentum-dependent spin sources, the authors predict measurable transverse spin textures. This offers an atomic platform to study fundamental physics governing spin generation in structured quantum media.
main_problem: The research aims to demonstrate programmable spin conversion mechanisms within gradient quantum matter systems.
main_result: A dissipative-curvature mechanism generates a controllable spin source whose transverse momentum texture is parity-locked to the applied drive and programmed gradient curvature.
method: The analysis uses quantum kinetic theory, employing the Wigner transform and expanding the collision integral to second order in spatial gradients.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a two-component ultracold Fermi gas, serving as an analog for gradient quantum materials. The dynamics are governed by spin-matrix distribution functions derived from the Kadanoff-Baym equation.
key_observables: Spin-resolved time-of-flight imaging revealing transverse spin textures; momentum-weighted projections of source terms ($K_{X}^a$, $	ext{D}_a^z$).
important_parameters: Coherent shift ($\Lambda$) and dissipative rates ($\Gamma$); the magnitude and spatial variation of these self-energies.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on local Markov approximation and expanding kinetic terms up to second order in spatial gradients.
figures_summary: FIG. 1 illustrates how a drive crossing a dissipative region causes scalar-to-spin conversion, resulting in measurable transverse spin imbalance (+z vs -z).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by deriving the kinetic equation for spin components using Wigner transforms, separating contributions from coherent gradients ($\Lambda$) and dissipative curvatures ($\Gamma$), and finally analyzing momentum-integrated source terms to predict observable spin textures.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework connecting controllable parameters in ultracold atomic systems (like spatial variations in interaction/potential) directly to measurable non-equilibrium spin phenomena analogous to those studied in solid-state spintronics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Programmable gradient quantum spin material in a two-component cold-atom gas. A spin-independent drive Fx carries atoms through a tube-shaped cloud crossed by a finite- thickness dissipative region with nonuniform spin-dependent Γa(r). The incoming components are mixed. After crossing the region, the distribution is biased, with the +a-polarized atoms (orange) preferentially on the +z side and the −a- polarized atoms (blue) on the −z side. This transverse spin imbalance illustrates scalar-to-spin conversion, the cold-atom analog of charge-to-spin conversion in an electronic gradient material.

Spin-momentum entanglement.note: The main result describes a 'transverse momentum texture' generated by spin conversion, directly addressing the correlation between internal (spin) and external/motional (momentum) degrees of freedom.
